title: The Africa Pivot: India and Japan’s Quest for Critical Mineral Security
author: Varuna Shankar
text:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sane to Hyderabad House, New Delhi, India, July 2, 2026.
Credit: Indian Ministry of External Affairs
A new axis is emerging in the global race for resources, and the Indian Ocean serves as a bridge. It is emerging as a critical corridor linking Africa’s mineral wealth to Asia’s industrial ambitions. Africa sits at one end of a strategic corridor, and its minerals are becoming the new terrain of strategic competition. The continent is home to critical minerals essential for the global energy transition, including 55 percent of the world’s cobalt, 47.65 percent of its manganese, 21.6 percent of its graphite, 5.9 percent of its copper, and 0.6 percent of its iron ore. Africa is already emerging as a priority in ongoing India-Japan discussions on economic security and supply chains and, as the India-Japan leaders’ recent summit and the subsequent India-Japan Joint Declaration on Economic Security Cooperation confirmed, it now sits squarely within the partnership’s formal architecture. Backed by the India-Japan Joint Economic Forum, a new JETRO strategic report, and renewed focus on the Asia-Africa Growth Corridor (AAGC), India and Japan are positioning themselves to deepen cooperation in critical minerals, digital infrastructure, healthcare, green energy, and resilient supply chains across the Global South, seeing it as an opportunity for the next phase of investment. At the heart of this push is Africa, where the race for critical minerals is reshaping economic partnerships into long-term strategic leverage.[...]
